explanation:
The theorem says the library's `adeleBddPrincipal` (a sup of two comaps along `(adeleSpace K F).subtype`) equals the comap of the sup. It is about the library's own definitions (`adeleBdd`, `globalSub`, `adeleSpace`, `adeleBddPrincipal`). The proof applies `Submodule.comap_subtype_sup_of_le_of_le`, which belongs to the library, not to Mathlib. That lemma says: for S, T ≤ C, comap C.subtype S ⊔ comap C.subtype T = comap C.subtype (S ⊔ T).

I searched Mathlib for a Submodule version of this fact under the names `comap_sup*`, `comap_subtype_sup*`, `comap_sup_eq*` and `sup_comap_eq`. Mathlib only has it for subgroups, as `Subgroup.comap_sup_eq_of_le_range`. For submodules it has only related but different lemmas: `Submodule.comap_sup_map_of_injective` and `Submodule.comap_map_sup_of_comap_le`. None of these gives the statement as a direct instantiation. In any case the substance of the theorem lies in the library's own adele definitions.
